title_zh: 连环画《三国演义03：捉放曹》
title_en: Comic Book 'Romance of the Three Kingdoms 03: Capture and Release of Cao Cao'
source_file: 连环画《三国演义03：捉放曹》（7-11岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 捉放曹
捉放曹
（三国演义之三）
陆士达 改编
徐正平 绘画

[P2] 内容提要
上集“董卓进京”，叙董卓乘乱废立，独掌朝廷大权。
本集叙曹操谋刺董卓未成，逃出京城，在中牟县被县令陈宫捉住。陈宫钦佩他的忠义，弃了官职，与他同逃。逃到成皋地方，多疑的曹操错杀了好心的吕伯奢全家。陈宫看出曹操心狠手辣，弃了他独自走了。
下集“虎牢关”，叙曹操回乡起兵，并召集十七镇诸侯，讨伐董卓。

1. 袁绍住在渤海，听说董卓弄权，便写了一封密信，派人到洛阳去，送给王允。

[P3] 2. 王允读完密信，原来袁绍责备他不能报国效忠，并要他找机会杀死董卓。王允考虑再三，也想不出主意来。
3. 有一天，王允上朝，在侍班阁子内看到一些旧臣都在，便道：“今日是老夫生日，晚间请诸位到我家小酌。”众官都道：“我们一定来替你老祝寿。”

[P4] 4. 到了晚上，王允在后堂摆酒。不一会儿，那些官员们都陆续到来。
5. 酒吃了几杯，王允忽然掩面大哭起来。众官都很惊奇，问道：‘司徒的生日，正该高高兴兴的庆祝一番，怎么竟伤起心来了？’

[P5] 6. 王允说：“董卓祸国殃民，社稷早晚难保。想不到汉朝天下，传到今天，竟丧在董卓之手，我怎能不痛心呢！”众官听了，也都掩面哭泣，但谁也想不出一个对付董卓的好办法来。

7. 大家正在悲愤的时候，忽然有个人仰面大笑起来。王允抬头一看，他是骁骑校尉曹操。

哈哈！你们夜哭到明，明哭到夜，难道还能哭死董卓不成？

[P6] 8. 王允气冲冲地责问曹操：“你也是朝廷官员，这种时候还不图报答国家，反笑些什么？”曹操说：“我笑的是这么多大官，竟想不出一个杀掉董卓之计！……”王允连忙离座请教。
9. 曹操说：“我早有心杀掉董卓，近来对他奉承，就是为了骗取信任，以便找个机会行刺。听说司徒有口七星宝刀，请借给我，拼死干他一下！”王允喜出望外，便亲自斟了杯酒给他。

[P7] 10. 王允随即把七星宝刀拿出来，亲自交给曹操。
11. 第二天，曹操带着宝刀，来到相府门前下马。侍卫知道他是董卓心腹，就把他放了进去。

[P8] 12. 曹操走进相府，听说董卓在小阁中，便寻向小阁而来。

13. 曹操到了小阁，只见董卓坐在榻上，正和吕布说话。他觉得吕布在旁，难以下手。心里暗暗发愁，也只得上前行礼。

我骑的一匹瘦马走不快，所以来迟了。

孟德，你今天怎么来得这样晚？

[P9] 14. 董卓听说曹操骑的是瘦马，便叫吕布去拣一匹西凉进贡来的好马，赏给曹操。
15. 吕布走后，曹操暗喜：“老贼该死了！”正要拔出刀来，转念一想：“老贼力大，硬来不行。”不觉踌躇起来。

[P10] 16. 董卓身体肥胖，坐了一会儿，感到疲倦，就倒身朝里睡下。曹操见机会已到，赶忙拔出刀来。
17. 他鼓足勇气，正要下手，不料董卓从镜里看到曹操在背后拔刀，猛的一个翻身，喝道：“孟德干吗？”

[P11] 18. 这时外边又传来马嘶声，吕布已牵马到了阁下。曹操惊慌之下，情急智生，忙把刀一捧，上前跪下说：‘我有一口宝刀，特来献给恩相。’
19. 董卓接过刀来一看：这刀一尺多长，七宝嵌镶，寒光闪闪，非常锋利。他只顾欣赏那口宝刀，却没有注意曹操惊慌的神色。

[P12] 20. 这时，吕布走了进来，董卓便把刀交给他收藏。曹操顺水推舟，解下刀鞘，递给吕布。
21. 董卓领着曹操出阁看马。只见那马浑身雪白，头高尾长，四个大蹄不住地在地上踢踏，果然是一匹好马。曹操故意称赞一番，要求骑上一试，董卓答应了。

[P13] 对！
22. 曹操走后，吕布对董卓说：“我看曹操刚才的神色有些不对哩。”这话把董卓提醒，心里也疑惑起来。
23. 正说间，李儒进来。董卓把这事说了一遍，李儒说：“这事容易弄明白。马上差个人去唤曹操，如果来了，那是真心献刀；如推托不来，定是行刺，就可以把他抓起来。”

[P14] 24. 董卓认为李儒的话有道理，立刻差了四名狱卒去唤曹操。狱卒们到了曹操寓府，见里面空空的，连家眷也没有一个。
25. 狱卒们再到城门口来查问。门吏道：‘刚才曹操走过这儿。他说：‘丞相差我有紧急公事。’一出城，就纵马去了！’

[P15] 26. 狱卒们只好回报董卓。李儒道：“曹贼心虚逃窜，定是行刺无疑了。”

我料定还有同谋的人，必须捉住曹操，审问明白，把他们一网打尽。

快快行文各地，谁能捉住曹操，赏十金，封万户侯；窝藏的同罪！

27. 董卓气得暴跳如雷。说道：“我如此重用他，他反要来害我！”便叫李儒立即画影图形，行文各地，捉拿曹操。

[P16] 28. 董卓派了快马，命各州、各县把捉拿曹操的图形，张贴在四门。
29. 再说，曹操诓出东门，一连几鞭，飞奔而去。

[P17] 30. 曹操一路往谯郡老家奔去；他恐董卓派人追捕，只拣小路，日夜赶程。
31. 这天，路过中牟县，天色已晚，他又累又饿，只得大着胆子，牵马进城。想在城里买些吃食，找个客店歇一夜再走。

[P18] 32. 不料走近城门，守门的兵士看到他的面貌和图形一模一样，就认出他是曹操，立刻围上前来把他捉住。

33. 兵士们把曹操解到县衙，县令陈宫立刻坐堂审问。曹操谎说自己是个过路客商。陈宫仔细望了望他，捉摸了好一会儿，最后还是说破了他。

我在洛阳求官的时候，就认得你了，怎么还抵赖呢！

我是姓皇甫，是过路的客商。

[P19] 34. 陈宫吩咐狱卒：‘把曹操关起来，明天解京请赏！’曹操无计可施，愤慨地长叹一声，跟着狱卒走了。
35. 陈宫退堂之后，心里非常作难：原来他也痛恨董卓祸国殃民，认为曹操大胆行刺，是英雄豪杰的作为，有意要释放他。但又怕董卓知道要连累自己……左思右想，主意难定。

[P20] 不能叫天下人骂
我贪图富贵……对！
来人哪！带曹操！
36. 最后他想：“如果把曹操解进京去，定会遭天下人唾骂，不如把他叫来，细细探问一番，若是个真英雄，自己拼却县官不做，就跟他一起走……”主意打定，就叫差役带人。
37. 半夜时分，曹操被带到后堂。陈宫故意问道：“董丞相待你不薄，你为何要自找祸害？”曹操冷笑一声：“庸官俗吏，哪知英雄豪杰的志气！你既拿住了我，就该解去请赏，何必多说！”，

[P21] 38. 陈宫听了，并没动气，就对两边差役说道：“我要细细审问曹操，你们且退出去。”差役应诺而去。
39. 屋里只剩下他们两人。陈宫便说：“曹操，可别自命英雄，瞧不起人，我也并不是那种庸官俗吏！”曹操明白了陈宫的心意，不禁喜出望外，就激昂地把自己的志愿说了一番。
如果放了你，你有什么打算？
能放我回家，我一定约天下诸侯，共起义兵，讨伐董贼！

[P22] 好在我老母妻子，都在东都，就此一起走吧！
40. 陈宫更加心服，马上给曹操开了刑具，扶到椅上坐了，纳头便拜；一边说明自己也有报国之心，决定与他弃官同走。曹操大喜，慌忙回拜。
41. 陈宫当即收拾盘费，和曹操一起换了衣服，各背宝剑一口，骑马逃走。守关兵士见是县令，也不盘问，就开了城门放他们走了。

[P23] 42. 两人一路奔往谯郡。这天，来到成皋地方，天色将晚，曹操要到他父亲的结义兄弟吕伯奢家里借宿一宵，就便探问家中消息。陈宫也说很好，两匹马就向吕家庄走去。
43. 到了庄前，下马叫门，出来一位慈眉善目的老翁。曹操口称伯父，连忙行礼。

[P24] 是小侄的好友，中牟县令陈宫。
……哦！这位是谁？
44. 吕伯奢一见曹操，就惊喜地说：“听说官家出了重赏捉你，你的父亲已躲到陈留去了，我正替你担心……”说着，一眼看见陈宫，马上把话缩了回去。曹操会意，忙把陈宫介绍给他。
45. 进了草堂，曹操把经过说了一遍。伯奢听了，非常感激陈宫，向他拜谢道：“若非使君搭救，小侄早没命了！”陈宫也谦逊了一番。

[P25] 46. 谈了一会，伯奢起身说：‘使君、贤侄宽心，就在这里宿一宵吧。’说完，进到里边去了。
47. 好一会，吕伯奢走了出来，对客人说：‘家里没有好酒待客，我且到西村去沽一点来。’说罢，跨上小驴，匆匆就走。

[P26] 我和他究竟不是至亲，他去沽酒，形迹可疑，我们到里边去听听！
48. 两人等了好久，忽听得一阵霍霍的磨刀声。曹操暗吃一惊，想起刚才吕伯奢去沽酒时匆促的神情，不禁疑惑起来。
49. 两个人轻轻走到里边，只听得有人在说：“捆了杀吧？”曹操忙对陈宫说：“你听！果然是要算计我们了。若不抢先下手，我们就要遭殃。”

[P27] 50. 说罢，拔剑冲了进去，见人便杀。
51. 曹操一连杀了男女八口，最后搜到厨房，却见一只肥猪，捆倒地上。陈宫恍然大悟道：“孟德多疑，错杀好人了！”

[P28] 52. 曹操说：“杀已杀了，还说什么，快走吧！
53. 这时，天已黑了，四下里静悄悄的不见一人。陈宫随着曹操，仓皇上马，出庄而去。

[P29] 说什么！
有我哩！
不好！吕伯奢回来了，还是躲一躲吧！
54. 走不到两里，就听得前边蹄声得得，有人走了过来。陈宫心里一阵着慌，就想往斜刺里躲，却被曹操拦住。
55. 来人愈来愈近，看出是吕伯奢骑着小驴，提着果菜，驴鞍上挂着一个酒葫芦，一路催着牲口过来。

[P30] 56. 吕伯奢迎面见了陈宫和曹操，不禁诧问：“贤侄、使君！怎么这就走了？”曹操冷冷答道：“有罪之人，不敢久留。”
57. 伯奢下了驴子，再三挽留。陈宫听了他恳切的言词，更不敢回头看他一眼，心里只是替他难过。曹操不管这些，打马就走。
我已经叫家里杀了一口猪，还赶了许多路，沽得两壶好酒，贤侄，使君，快请回来！

[P31] 58. 走不几步，曹操忽然拔出宝剑，回过身来向伯奢叫道：“那边来的是谁？”吕伯奢以为真有人来，便回过头去。
59. 曹操乘他不防，猛力一剑砍去，只见吕伯奢没出一声就倒在驴下。陈宫万想不到曹操竟会出此毒手，一声惊叫，几乎跌下马来。

[P32] 60. 陈宫问道：“刚才是误杀，现在却是为了什么啊？”曹操说：“伯奢到家，见杀死多人，怎肯罢休。如果领人来追赶，一定要受累了。”
61. 陈宫叹息道：“知而故杀，这是大不应该的。”曹操道：“斩草就要除根！我曹操一生做事，就欢喜干干净净。宁可我负天下人，不教天下人负我！”

[P33] 62. 陈宫听了，心冷如冰。回头看看，吕伯奢倒在血泊中，果菜、酒葫芦散了一地，心里更觉难过，忍不住滚鞍下马，对着尸体流泪。
63. 曹操连声催他上马。陈宫没奈何，只得忍气吞声，跟着连夜赶路。

[P34] 64. 又走了十多里，只见月光中有一家客店。曹操上前敲门。
65. 店东开了门，让他们住下。两人匆匆吃喝完了，喂饱马匹，曹操先自睡了。陈宫因为心里有事，再不想睡。

[P35] 66. 直到三更时分，陈宫还靠在桌上，心乱如麻。他懊悔自己不该冒失地弃官跟从曹操，弄到现在进退两难。跟他走吧？心里厌恶透了，怎么也不愿意；离开他吧？又怕没处抽身，给董卓捉住，性命不保。
67. 他正打不定主意，回头看看曹操，却睡得鼻息如雷。陈宫又想：‘这人心肠狠毒，如果将来得势，也是百姓的祸害。不如乘他这时睡着，一剑砍死。’他心肠一横，拔出宝剑，向曹操颈上砍去……

[P36] 68. 猛地，他又想：“我原是为国家大事跟他来到这里，如果这时暗杀了他，岂非不义！”想到这里，又把剑缩了回来；于是打定主意，丢了曹操，一人逃走。
69. 曹操一觉醒来，不见了陈宫，暗想：“此人叫我说了两句，疑我不仁，因而丢下我独个儿跑了。看这情形，这地方不能再呆下去了。”

[P37] 70. 曹操匆匆出店上马，一溜烟逃奔陈留去。
71. 回到陈留家中，向父亲曹嵩诉说京城情况，打算变卖家资，招募义兵，讨伐董卓。

[P38] 72. 曹嵩沉吟好久，觉得家资短少，不够招兵之用。说本地有一姓卫名弘的孝廉是个巨富，而且肯仗义疏财，可以找他帮忙。
73. 曹操摆下酒席，恭请卫弘到家。对他说：“现在汉室无主，董卓专权，欺君害民，百姓恨之入骨。我打算招募义兵，挽救社稷，只恨力量不足，久闻先生忠心义胆，愿求相助。”

[P39] 74. 卫弘道：‘我早有这个心事了，只恨没有遇着英雄罢了。既孟德（曹操的号）有大志，愿出家资相助。’
75. 曹操大喜，招待卫弘吃过酒饭以后，立刻动手写了一道矫诏（诈称皇帝的诏书），大意是天子密令曹操讨伐董卓，望各路诸侯相助。写好后，曹操派家丁分送各地。

[P40] 76. 然后开始招集义兵，并在家门前竖起一面招兵的旗，上面写着“忠义”两个大字。
77. 应募的人非常踊跃。精通武艺的如乐进、李典、夏侯惇、夏侯渊、族弟曹仁、曹洪等人，纷纷前来投效。

[P41] 78. 曹操在村中调练军马。卫弘拿出所有家财，置办衣甲旗帜。各处送粮食来的不记其数。
79. 不久，渤海太守袁绍接得曹操送来的矫诏，便率领部下的文官武将，士兵三万人，离开渤海，来和曹操相会。

[P42] 80. 两个人商谈了一阵，袁绍见各路诸侯并无动静，要曹操再发一道檄文。曹操立刻起草，上面写道：“操等谨以大义，布公天下，董卓灭国弑君，残害生灵……今奉天子密诏，大集义兵，誓欲扫清华夏，剿戮群凶，望兴义师，共汇公愤……”
81. 写好檄文，曹操派了十几名家丁分头驰送给各路诸侯，请他们从速起兵响应。欲知后事，请看下集《虎牢关》
full_text_en:
[P1] Catching and Releasing Cao
Catching and Releasing Cao
(The Third of Romance of the Three Kingdoms)
Adapted by Lu Shida
Illustrated by Xu Zhengping

[P2] Content Summary
The previous volume, "Dong Zhuo Enters the Capital," narrates how Dong Zhuo seized power during the chaos, deposed the emperor, and took control of the imperial court.
This volume tells of Cao Cao's failed assassination attempt on Dong Zhuo. He fled the capital and was captured by County Magistrate Chen Gong in Zhongmu County. Impressed by Cao Cao's loyalty and righteousness, Chen Gong resigned his official post and fled with him. When they reached Chenggao, the suspicious Cao Cao mistakenly killed the entire family of the kind-hearted Lü Boshu. Chen Gong realized Cao Cao was ruthless and cruel, and left him alone.
The next volume, "Hulao Pass," narrates Cao Cao returning to his hometown to raise troops and gathering seventeen allied warlords to campaign against Dong Zhuo.

1. Yuan Shao, residing in Bohai, heard that Dong Zhuo was seizing power, so he wrote a secret letter and sent someone to Luoyang to deliver it to Wang Yun.

[P3] 2. Wang Yun finished reading the secret letter. It turned out that Yuan Shao blamed him for failing to be loyal to the country and demanded that he find an opportunity to kill Dong Zhuo. Wang Yun thought about it again and again, but couldn't come up with any idea.
3. One day, Wang Yun went to court. Seeing some old ministers in the waiting hall, he said, "Today is my birthday. I invite you all to my home for a small drink in the evening." The officials all replied, "We will certainly come to celebrate your birthday, sir."

[P4] 4. In the evening, Wang Yun set up a banquet in the back hall. In no time, the officials arrived one after another.
5. After a few cups of wine, Wang Yun suddenly covered his face and burst into tears. The officials were very surprised and asked, 'Today is the Grand Tutor's birthday. We should be celebrating joyfully. Why are you so sad?'

[P5] 6. Wang Yun said, "Dong Zhuo is harming the country and its people; the state is in danger. I never thought that the Han dynasty, passed down to today, would fall into Dong Zhuo's hands. How could I not be heartbroken?" The officials, upon hearing this, also covered their faces and wept, but none could think of a good way to deal with Dong Zhuo.

7. Just as everyone was filled with sorrow and anger, suddenly someone burst into loud laughter, head thrown back. Wang Yun looked up and saw that it was Cao Cao, the Commander of the Cavalry.

Ha ha! You cry all night, then cry all day, and then cry all night again. Do you really think you can cry Dong Zhuo to death?

[P6] 8. Wang Yun angrily scolded Cao Cao: "You are also an official of the court. At such a time, you don't even think of repaying the country, yet you laugh?" Cao Cao replied: "I laugh at how so many high-ranking officials can't even come up with a plan to kill Dong Zhuo! ..." Wang Yun immediately rose from his seat to seek his advice.
9. Cao Cao said: "I've long wanted to kill Dong Zhuo. Recently, I've been flattering him to gain his trust, so I can find an opportunity to assassinate him. I've heard that the Minister of Works has a Seven-Star Saber. Please lend it to me, and I'll risk my life to strike him down!" Wang Yun was overjoyed and personally poured a cup of wine for him.

[P7] 10. Wang Yun immediately took out the Seven-Star Saber and personally handed it to Cao Cao.
11. The next day, Cao Cao, carrying the saber, arrived at the chancellor's mansion and dismounted. The guards, knowing he was a close aide of Dong Zhuo, let him in.

[P8] 12. Cao Cao entered the prime minister's residence. Hearing that Dong Zhuo was in a small pavilion, he headed toward it.

13. Cao Cao arrived at the pavilion and saw Dong Zhuo sitting on a couch, talking with Lu Bu. He felt that with Lu Bu present, it would be hard to act. He was deeply troubled but had no choice but to bow respectfully.

I rode a thin horse that couldn't go fast, so I arrived late.

Mengde, why are you so late today?

[P9] 14. Dong Zhuo heard that Cao Cao was riding a thin horse, so he ordered Lu Bu to pick out a fine horse from the tribute of Xiliang and give it to Cao Cao.
15. After Lu Bu left, Cao Cao secretly rejoiced: "The old traitor should die!" He was about to draw his knife, but then thought: "The old traitor is strong; brute force won't work." He hesitated unconsciously.

[P10] 16. Dong Zhuo, whose body was fat, sat for a while, felt tired, and then lay down facing inward. Cao Cao saw his chance and quickly drew his knife.
17. He mustered his courage and was about to strike, but unexpectedly, Dong Zhuo saw Cao Cao drawing the knife from behind in the mirror, and suddenly flipped over, shouting, "Mengde, what are you doing?"

[P11] 18. At this moment, the sound of a horse neighing came from outside; Lü Bu had already led his horse to the pavilion. In panic, Cao Cao, thinking quickly, hurriedly held up the sword and knelt down, saying, 'I have a precious sword, specially brought to present to my esteemed chancellor.'
19. Dong Zhuo took the sword and examined it: it was over a foot long, inlaid with seven treasures, gleaming coldly, and extremely sharp. He was only absorbed in admiring the sword and did not notice Cao Cao's panicked expression.

[P12] 20. At this moment, Lü Bu walked in, and Dong Zhuo handed the sword over to him for safekeeping. Cao Cao, seizing the opportunity, took off the scabbard and handed it to Lü Bu.
21. Dong Zhuo led Cao Cao out of the hall to view the horses. The horse was pure white, with a tall head and long tail, its four large hooves kicking and stomping on the ground — clearly a fine steed. Cao Cao deliberately praised it and asked to ride it, and Dong Zhuo agreed.

[P13] Right!
22. After Cao Cao left, Lu Bu said to Dong Zhuo, "I think Cao Cao's expression just now was a bit off." These words awakened Dong Zhuo, who began to feel suspicious.
23. Just as they were talking, Li Ru came in. Dong Zhuo told him what had happened. Li Ru said, "This is easy to figure out. Send someone immediately to summon Cao Cao. If he comes, he is sincerely offering the sword; if he refuses to come, he must be planning an assassination, and we can arrest him then."

[P14] 24. Dong Zhuo thought Li Ru's words made sense, and immediately sent four jailers to summon Cao Cao. The jailers arrived at Cao Cao's residence and found it empty, not even a single family member present.
25. The jailers then went to the city gate to inquire. The gatekeeper said, 'Cao Cao just passed by here. He said, 'The Chancellor has urgent business for me.' As soon as he left the city, he galloped off!'

[P15] 26. The jailers could only report back to Dong Zhuo. Li Ru said, "Cao the traitor fled in fear; it's certain he attempted assassination.

I am sure there are accomplices. We must capture Cao Cao, interrogate them, and catch them all.

Quickly issue orders to all regions: whoever captures Cao Cao will be rewarded with ten gold coins and granted the title of Marquis of Ten Thousand Households; those who harbor him will be punished equally!

27. Dong Zhuo was furious and jumped up like thunder. He said, "I trusted and favored him so much, yet he dared to try to harm me!" He then ordered Li Ru to immediately draw a wanted poster and issue orders throughout the regions to capture Cao Cao.

[P16] 28. Dong Zhuo sent messengers on fast horses, ordering all provinces and counties to post wanted posters of Cao Cao at the four city gates.
29. Meanwhile, Cao Cao slipped out of the eastern gate, whipped his horse several times, and galloped away.

[P17] 30. Cao Cao hurried toward his hometown in Qiao Commandery; fearing that Dong Zhuo would send men to pursue him, he took only small paths and traveled day and night.
31. That day, passing through Zhongmu County, it was already dark. He was tired and hungry, so he plucked up his courage, led his horse into the city, and planned to buy some food and find an inn to rest for the night before continuing.

[P18] 32. Unluckily, as he approached the city gate, the guards saw his face matched the wanted poster exactly, recognized him as Cao Cao, and immediately surrounded and captured him.

33. The soldiers took Cao Cao to the county衙 (yé, office), where Magistrate Chen Gong immediately began questioning him. Cao Cao lied, claiming he was just a traveling merchant. Chen Gong looked at him carefully, pondered for a while, and finally exposed him.

I knew you when I was seeking office in Luoyang. Why are you still denying it?

I am surnamed Huangfu, a traveling merchant.

[P19] 34. Chen Gong ordered the jailer: 'Lock Cao Cao up and send him to the capital tomorrow for reward!' Cao Cao, with no other options, sighed bitterly and followed the jailer.
35. After leaving the courtroom, Chen Gong was deeply conflicted: he too hated Dong Zhuo for bringing disaster to the country and its people, and believed Cao Cao's bold assassination attempt was the act of a heroic and outstanding man, so he intended to release him. But he also feared that if Dong Zhuo found out, he would be implicated... He thought and thought, unable to make up his mind.

[P20] Can't let the world curse me
For greed and wealth... Right!
Bring me Cao Cao!
36. Finally, he thought: "If I send Cao Cao to the capital, I'll surely be cursed by the world. Better to bring him here, question him carefully. If he's a true hero, I'll give up my county magistrate position and go with him..." Having made up his mind, he called the guards to bring him.
37. In the middle of the night, Cao Cao was brought to the back hall. Chen Gong deliberately asked: "Dong Zhuang treated you well, why did you bring disaster upon yourself?" Cao Cao laughed coldly: "Ordinary officials and petty clerks, how could they understand the aspirations of heroes and great men! Since you've caught me, you should take me to claim the reward. Why say more!"

[P21] 38. Chen Gong listened, but did not get angry. He told the guards on both sides, "I want to interrogate Cao Cao carefully. You may leave for now." The guards nodded and left.
39. Only the two of them remained in the room. Chen Gong said, "Cao Cao, don't think yourself a hero and look down on others. I am not the kind of petty official or vulgar bureaucrat!" Cao Cao understood Chen Gong's intention, and was overjoyed. He then passionately spoke about his aspirations.
If I let you go, what are your plans?
If you let me return home, I will surely gather the feudal lords of the realm, raise a righteous army, and讨伐董贼! (If you let me return home, I will surely gather the feudal lords of the realm, raise a righteous army, and punish Dong Zhuo!)

[P22] Good thing my mother and wife are in the Eastern Capital; let's go together!
40. Chen Gong was even more impressed. He immediately removed Cao Cao's restraints, helped him sit on a chair, and bowed deeply, explaining that he too had a heart for serving the country, and decided to resign his post and leave with him. Cao Cao was overjoyed and hurriedly returned the bow.
41. Chen Gong immediately gathered provisions, changed clothes with Cao Cao, each took a sword, and rode away. The guards at the gate, seeing that he was the county magistrate, did not question them and opened the gate to let them go.

[P23] 42. The two rode on toward Qiao Commandery. That day, arriving at Chenggao, as dusk fell, Cao Cao wanted to stay overnight at the home of his father's sworn brother, Lü Boshu, and also inquire about his family's news. Chen Gong agreed, and the two horses headed toward Lü's village.
43. Upon reaching the village gate, they dismounted and knocked on the door. An elderly man with kind eyes came out. Cao Cao called him 'Uncle' and hurriedly bowed.

[P24] This is my nephew's good friend, Chen Gong, the county magistrate of Zhongmu.
... Oh! Who is this?
44. When Lü Boshu saw Cao Cao, he was delighted and said, "I heard the authorities have put a heavy reward on your head, and your father has already fled to Chenliu. I was worried about you..." But as he glanced and saw Chen Gong, he immediately stopped speaking. Cao Cao understood and quickly introduced Chen Gong to him.
45. Inside the thatched hall, Cao Cao recounted the entire story. Upon hearing it, Boshu was deeply grateful to Chen Gong and bowed to him, saying, "If it were not for your rescue, my nephew would have been dead long ago!" Chen Gong modestly replied.

[P25] 46. After talking for a while, Bo She stood up and said, 'Master, dear nephew, please rest easy. Stay here for the night.' Then he went inside.
47. After a while, Lü Bo She came out and said to the guests, 'I don't have good wine at home to entertain you. I'll go to the village to the west to buy some.' Saying that, he mounted his donkey and hurried off.

[P26] I and he are not close relatives. He went to buy wine, his behavior is suspicious. Let's go inside and listen!
48. The two waited for a long time, when suddenly they heard the sound of a knife being sharpened. Cao Cao was startled, recalling the hurried expression of Lü Boshua when he left to buy wine, and became suspicious.
49. The two quietly approached the inner part, and heard someone saying, "Tie them up and kill them!" Cao Cao hurriedly told Chen Gong, "Listen! They are indeed plotting against us. If we don't strike first, we will be in danger."

[P27] 50. Saying that, he drew his sword and charged in, killing anyone he saw.
51. Cao Cao killed eight men and women in succession. Finally, searching the kitchen, he saw a fat pig tied up and lying on the ground. Chen Gong suddenly realized and said, "Mengde is too suspicious; you've killed innocent people!"

[P28] 52. Cao Cao said: "They're already dead, what's the point of talking? Let's go quickly!"
53. At this time, it was already dark, and everything around was quiet and empty. Chen Gong followed Cao Cao, hurriedly mounted the horse, and left the village.

[P29] What's the matter!
I'm here!
Oh no! Lü Boshua is coming back, let's hide for a moment!
54. Not even two li away, they heard hoofbeats coming from ahead. Chen Gong became anxious and tried to dodge into the side, but was stopped by Cao Cao.
55. As the person drew closer, they saw it was Lü Boshua riding a small donkey, carrying fruits and vegetables, with a wine gourd hanging on the donkey's saddle, urging the beast forward.

[P30] 56. Lü Boshua met Chen Gong and Cao Cao face to face and asked in surprise, "Dear nephew, Lord! Why are you leaving so soon?" Cao Cao coldly replied, "A guilty man dares not stay long." 
57. Boshua dismounted from his donkey and tried to persuade them to stay repeatedly. Chen Gong, hearing his sincere words, dared not even turn to look at him, feeling only sorrow for him. Cao Cao paid no heed and spurred his horse to leave.
I have already asked my family to slaughter a pig, traveled a long way, and bought two jars of fine wine. Dear nephew, Lord, please come back quickly!

[P31] 58. After walking only a few steps, Cao Cao suddenly drew his sword, turned around, and called out to Lü Boshang, 'Who is coming from over there?' Lü Boshang, thinking someone was truly approaching, turned his head.
59. Taking advantage of his unpreparedness, Cao Cao struck fiercely with his sword. Lü Boshang fell silent beneath the donkey. Chen Gong, utterly shocked that Cao Cao would commit such a ruthless act, let out a cry and nearly fell off his horse.

[P32] 60. Chen Gong asked, "It was a mistaken killing just now, but what is the reason for this now?" Cao Cao said, "When Bo She returns home and sees so many people killed, how could he possibly let it go? If he leads people to chase us, we will surely be in trouble." 
61. Chen Gong sighed, "To kill knowingly is greatly wrong." Cao Cao said, "When cutting grass, one must remove the roots! I, Cao Cao, have always liked to do things cleanly. I would rather betray the whole world than let the whole world betray me!"

[P33] 62. Chen Gong listened, his heart as cold as ice. Looking back, he saw Lü Boshu lying in a pool of blood, fruits, vegetables, and wine gourds scattered on the ground. He felt even more sorrowful, couldn't help dismounting, and wept over the body.
63. Cao Cao urged him to get back on horse. Chen Gong had no choice but to grit his teeth and follow, hurrying on the road through the night.

[P34] 64. After traveling more than ten li, they saw an inn in the moonlight. Cao Cao went forward to knock on the door.
65. The innkeeper opened the door and let them stay. After hastily finishing their meal and feeding the horses, Cao Cao went to sleep first. Chen Gong, troubled by his thoughts, could not sleep.

[P35] 66. Until the third watch, Chen Gong still leaned against the table, his heart in turmoil. He regretted having rashly abandoned his official post to follow Cao Cao, leaving him now in a dilemma. To go with him? He detested him deeply and could not bring himself to do so. To leave him? He feared having nowhere to flee, and being caught by Dong Zhuo, risking his life.
67. Still undecided, he turned to look at Cao Cao, who was sleeping soundly with loud snoring. Chen Gong thought: 'This man is cruel-hearted; if he ever gains power, he will be a disaster for the people. It would be better to kill him now while he sleeps.' He hardened his heart, drew his sword, and swung it toward Cao Cao's neck...

[P36] 68. Suddenly, he thought: 'I came here with him for the sake of national affairs. If I were to secretly kill him now, wouldn't that be unjust?' Thinking this, he pulled the sword back. He then made up his mind, left Cao Cao, and fled alone.
69. Cao Cao woke up and found Chen Gong was gone. He thought to himself: 'This man spoke to me a few words, suspected I was unkind, and thus left me alone. Given this situation, I can no longer stay here.'

[P37] 70. Cao Cao hurriedly left the inn, mounted his horse, and galloped off to Chenliu like a wisp of smoke.
71. Returning to his home in Chenliu, he told his father Cao Song about the situation in the capital, and planned to sell his family's assets, recruit volunteer troops, and campaign against Dong Zhuo.

[P38] 72. Cao Song pondered for a long time, feeling that his family's wealth was insufficient for recruiting soldiers. He mentioned that there was a wealthy scholar named Wei Hong in the area, who was generous and could be asked for help.
73. Cao Cao set up a banquet and respectfully invited Wei Hong to his home. He said to him, 'Now the Han dynasty has no ruler, Dong Zhuo holds power, oppresses the emperor and harms the people, and the common folk hate him to the bone. I plan to recruit righteous troops to save the nation, but I regret my limited strength. I have long heard of your loyalty and courage, and I humbly seek your assistance.'

[P39] 74. Wei Hong said: 'I've had this thought for a long time, I only regret not having met a hero yet. Since Mengde (Cao Cao's courtesy name) has great ambitions, I am willing to contribute my family's resources to help.'
75. Cao Cao was overjoyed. After entertaining Wei Hong with wine and food, he immediately wrote a forged edict (a false imperial decree), which stated that the emperor had secretly ordered Cao Cao to attack Dong Zhuo and requested aid from various warlords. After writing it, Cao Cao sent his servants to deliver the edict to various regions.

[P40] 76. Then he began to recruit volunteer soldiers and raised a recruitment banner in front of his home, with the two large characters 'Loyalty and Righteousness' written on it.
77. The number of people who responded was very enthusiastic. Skilled warriors such as Yue Jin, Li Dian, Xiahou Dun, Xiahou Yuan, and his cousins Cao Ren and Cao Hong came to join him one after another.

[P41] 78. Cao Cao trained his troops in a village. Wei Hong spent all his family wealth to procure armor and flags. Grain sent from various places was countless.
79. Soon after, Yuan Shao, the Governor of Bohai, received the forged imperial edict sent by Cao Cao, and led his civil and military officials, along with 30,000 soldiers, to leave Bohai and meet with Cao Cao.

[P42] 80. After discussing for a while, Yuan Shao, seeing that the various warlords had not taken any action, asked Cao Cao to issue another proclamation. Cao Cao immediately drafted it, which read: 'We, the undersigned, uphold righteousness and announce it to the world: Dong Zhuo has destroyed the state, murdered the sovereign, and harmed the people... Now, acting on the secret edict of the Son of Heaven, we gather righteous troops, swear to cleanse the realm of China, exterminate the wicked, and hope to raise a righteous army to share the public indignation...'
81. After writing the proclamation, Cao Cao sent several dozen household retainers to deliver it to the various warlords, urging them to quickly raise troops and respond. To learn what happens next, please read the next volume, 'Hulao Pass'.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《捉放曹》的封面，标明其为《三国演义》系列之三，由陆士达改编、徐正平绘画，并配有一幅描绘人物骑马行于溪流旁的插图。
[P2] 本页包含《捉放曹》的内容提要，概述了上集、本集和下集的主要情节，并以一幅插图和文字说明开头，讲述袁绍得知董卓专权后，写密信派人送往洛阳给王允。
[P3] 本页描绘了王允收到袁绍密信后陷入困境，以及他借生日之名邀请众官赴宴的情节。
[P4] 本页描绘了王允在后堂设宴，众官陆续到来后，王允在酒过几巡时突然掩面大哭，众官对此感到惊奇并询问原因。
[P5] 王允在宴会上痛陈董卓祸国殃民，众官悲泣却无计可施；此时曹操突然大笑，质疑仅靠哭泣无法除掉董卓。
[P6] 王允因曹操在宴会上大笑而责问，曹操解释自己早有杀董卓之心，并请求借七星宝刀行刺，王允听后大喜并亲自斟酒相待。
[P7] 本页描绘了王允将七星宝刀交给曹操，以及曹操次日携带宝刀前往相府，因被认作董卓心腹而顺利进入的情节。
[P8] 曹操前往相府行刺董卓，抵达小阁后发现董卓正与吕布交谈，因吕布在场而无法下手，只得上前行礼并以马慢为由解释迟到。
[P9] 本页描绘了曹操在董卓相府行刺的场景：董卓因曹操骑瘦马而赏赐好马，吕布离开后，曹操准备行刺但因顾虑董卓力大而踌躇不决。
[P10] 曹操在董卓相府行刺，趁董卓睡下时拔刀，但董卓从镜中发现后猛然翻身喝问，行刺失败。
[P11] 曹操在董卓相府行刺时，因吕布到来而惊慌，情急之下将宝刀献给董卓；董卓欣赏宝刀，未察觉曹操的惊慌神色。
[P12] 曹操在董卓相府行刺失败后，将宝刀献给吕布以示顺从；随后董卓带曹操出阁看马，曹操称赞并请求试骑，董卓答应。
[P13] 曹操行刺董卓失败后离开，吕布察觉其神色异常并提醒董卓，董卓心生疑虑；李儒进言建议召曹操前来，若其不来则定为行刺，可将其抓捕。
[P14] 董卓派狱卒去曹操府邸寻找曹操，发现府中空无一人；狱卒又到城门口询问，门吏称曹操以有紧急公事为由出城后便策马离去。
[P15] 狱卒回报曹操逃走，李儒断定其行刺，董卓大怒，命李儒画影图形，通缉曹操。
[P16] 本页描绘了董卓下令通缉曹操，张贴其画像于城门，同时曹操已策马逃离，飞奔而去。
[P17] 曹操为躲避董卓追捕，连夜赶路返回谯郡老家，途中路过中牟县时因天黑又累又饿，便牵马进城打算买些食物并找客栈歇息。
[P18] 曹操在逃亡途中被守门兵士认出并捉住，随后被押至中牟县衙，县令陈宫审问时，曹操谎称自己是过路客商，但被陈宫识破。
[P19] 曹操被陈宫下令关押，准备解往京城请赏；陈宫退堂后内心矛盾，既敬佩曹操的胆识，又担忧董卓报复，难以决断。
[P20] 陈宫在审问曹操后内心矛盾，最终决定不将曹操解往京城，而是将其带至后堂亲自探问。曹操被押至后堂，面对陈宫的质问，他表现出不屈的英雄气概，称庸官俗吏不懂英雄志气，直言应直接解去请赏。
[P21] 陈宫将差役遣退后，与曹操单独对话，询问其若被释放有何打算，曹操激昂表示将联合天下诸侯，起兵讨伐董卓。
[P22] 陈宫被曹操的志向打动，决定弃官与他一同逃走。两人换上便装，各背宝剑，趁夜骑马出城，守关兵士因认出陈宫是县令而未加阻拦。
[P23] 曹操与陈宫逃亡途中，来到成皋，决定前往曹操父亲的结义兄弟吕伯奢家借宿并探问家讯。两人抵达吕家庄前，曹操下马叩门，见到一位慈祥老翁，恭敬地称其为伯父并行礼。
[P24] 曹操与陈宫抵达吕伯奢家，吕伯奢见到曹操后惊喜万分，得知陈宫身份后连忙介绍。进屋后，曹操讲述逃亡经过，吕伯奢感激陈宫救命之恩，向其拜谢，陈宫谦逊回应。
[P25] 曹操与陈宫在吕伯奢家暂住，吕伯奢邀请他们留宿，并表示要去西村买酒款待。
[P26] 曹操与陈宫在吕伯奢家等待时，听到磨刀声，心生疑虑，潜入屋内偷听，发现有人密谋杀害他们，曹操判断对方有阴谋，决定抢先下手。
[P27] 曹操因怀疑吕伯奢家人图谋不轨，拔剑冲入屋内见人便杀，连杀八人；最后在厨房发现被捆倒的肥猪，陈宫恍然大悟，指出曹操错杀了好人。
[P28] 曹操在误杀吕伯奢家人后，催促陈宫立即离开。两人在夜色中仓皇骑马逃离吕家庄。
[P29] 曹操与陈宫逃亡途中，听到前方有蹄声，陈宫惊慌想躲，被曹操拦住。随后发现来人是骑着小驴、提着果菜的吕伯奢，正赶着牲口回来。
[P30] 曹操与陈宫在误杀吕伯奢家人后仓皇逃离，途中遇见归来的吕伯奢。吕伯奢热情挽留，称已杀猪备酒，但曹操因心怀愧疚与恐惧，执意不回头，策马离去。
[P31] 曹操在逃亡途中遇见归来的吕伯奢，假意询问后突然拔剑将其杀害，陈宫震惊不已。
[P32] 曹操在误杀吕伯奢家人后，为防报复，又将归来的吕伯奢杀害。陈宫对此表示震惊和惋惜，曹操则宣称‘宁可我负天下人，不教天下人负我’，表明其决绝冷酷的处世态度。
[P33] 陈宫目睹吕伯奢被杀后悲痛落泪，曹操则催促他上马，陈宫无奈只得忍痛跟随连夜逃亡。
[P34] 曹操与陈宫逃亡途中，在月光下找到一家客店，曹操敲门入住。两人吃完饭、喂饱马后，曹操先睡，陈宫因心事重重而无法入眠。
[P35] 陈宫在客店中彻夜难眠，内心挣扎于是否继续追随曹操。他最终决定趁曹操熟睡时将其杀死，但尚未下手，故事在此处中断。
[P36] 陈宫在客店中犹豫是否杀死熟睡的曹操，最终因顾念道义而放弃，独自逃走；曹操醒来后发现陈宫已离开，认为对方怀疑自己不仁，决定不再逗留。
[P37] 曹操逃离客店后，返回陈留家中，向父亲曹嵩报告京城情况，并计划变卖家产、招募义兵讨伐董卓。
[P38] 曹操返回陈留后，因家资不足，决定向富商卫弘求助。他设宴款待卫弘，陈述董卓专权、祸国殃民的现状，请求对方资助其招募义兵、挽救汉室。
[P39] 卫弘答应资助曹操讨伐董卓，曹操随即伪造皇帝诏书，命人分送各地以号召诸侯响应。
[P40] 曹操在陈留家中竖起写有“忠义”的招兵旗，开始招募义兵，许多武艺高强的人如乐进、李典、夏侯惇、夏侯渊、曹仁、曹洪等纷纷前来投效。
[P41] 曹操在村中训练军队，卫弘出资置办军需，各地纷纷送粮支援；不久后，袁绍接到曹操送来的矫诏，率领三万兵马离开渤海，前来与曹操会合。
[P42] 袁绍与曹操商议后，曹操起草并派家丁分送檄文，号召各路诸侯起兵讨伐董卓，故事将在《虎牢关》中继续。
